If we have a bunch of real numbers $a_1$, $a_2$, ..., $a_{n-1}$, $a_n$ and we want to add them all up, we can write that concisely with the familiar "big sigma" notation:

$$
\sum\limits_{i=1}^n a_i = a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_{n-1} + a_n.
$$

If instead we wish to *multiply* all of the numbers together, we can write that concisely with "big pi" notation, which is similar, but may be new to you:

$$
\prod\limits_{i=1}^na_i=a_1 \times a_2 \times ... \times a_{n-1} \times a_n.
$$

We use this a lot in statistics, so let's practice.

a. Let $c\in\mathbb{R}$ be any constant, and simplify this expression as much as possible:

$$
\prod\limits_{i=1}^nc\cdot a_i.
$$


b. Simplify this expression as much as possible:

$$
\ln\left(\prod\limits_{i=1}^ne^{a_i}\right).
$$
